cases.answer: The Hunan study does not report how many patients failed to undergo surgery after starting neoadjuvant therapy, or why. Patients who failed to undergo surgery for any reason were excluded, so only operated patients (190: 69 PD-1 plus chemotherapy, 121 chemotherapy alone) were analysed. The authors state that data on patients who failed to receive surgery were absent. Related information that does exist: one patient in each group was found unresectable during surgery because of advanced disease. Surgery was delayed beyond 42 days in 10 (14.5%) PD-1+Chemo patients and 14 (11.6%) Chemo patients. The 1–10% figures for failure to receive surgery come from other large multicenter studies, not this cohort.

cases.answer: In the Helsinki pembrolizumab cohort, 23 patients had a new troponin elevation, but only 11 (47.8% of those 23; 14.7% of the 75-patient pembrolizumab cohort) met the diagnostic criteria for ICI myocarditis. All of these cases were grade 1–2. The other 12 had a troponin rise that did not meet the criteria. Anthracycline was suspected in three of them and capecitabine in one. Possible ICI myocarditis was suspected in three on the basis of another autoimmune adverse event alone or with nonspecific ECG changes. In five the cause stayed unclear. Surveillance: ECG before the start of neoadjuvant therapy and troponin before every pembrolizumab cycle. Cardiac imaging was done if a test was abnormal or there were cardiac symptoms. Myocarditis was defined per ESC guidelines by a cardiologist. ICI myocarditis required a new troponin elevation plus either one major or two minor criteria. Pembrolizumab was permanently discontinued in all patients with troponin elevation.

cases.answer: No. The meta-analysis of RCTs found no significant association between ICIs and cardiac failure (RR 1.11, 95% CI 0.48–2.58, p = 0.80, 9 studies, 5,574 patients). A nonsignificant result means the study did not show an increased risk. It does not prove ICIs cannot cause heart failure, and the confidence interval is wide and includes both a lower risk and a more-than-doubled risk. The authors do not claim that proof. They note that myocarditis has an immune-linked etiology that can result in subsequent heart failure.

cases.answer: Among 3746 deaths in the SEER-Medicare cohort of older advanced-NSCLC patients on PD-1i (5076 patients), 85.34% were attributed to NSCLC and 2.80% to CVD. The 2.80% is 1.17% ischemic heart disease plus 1.63% other CVDs. Factors associated with higher CVD mortality in the Fine-Gray model were a history of CHF (sHR 2.10; 95% CI 1.37–3.21) and Medicaid dual eligibility vs private insurance (sHR 2.70; 95% CI 1.28–5.56). In the cause-specific Cox sensitivity analysis, age over 80 vs 65–69 was also a significant predictor (HR 2.50; 95% CI 1.08–5.77). PD-1i type (pembrolizumab vs nivolumab) was not associated with CVD mortality (sHR 1.08; 95% CI 0.63–1.84).
